etc/fr_os/dhcpcd6.conf.text:
# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64

etc/fr_os/dnsmasq_ra.conf.text:
# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# Router Advertisements on the LAN (ROADMAP FND-1b/1c), and nothing else:
# each device's /64s, for SLAAC -- the one dhcpcd gave it from the
# provider's prefix and the stable ULA one -- and, where the router's
# resolver serves the zone, the resolver's address (RDNSS).
# No DNS here: the ad-block resolver (fr-adblock-dns) answers it.
port=0
no-resolv
no-hosts
# Nothing is written: /run is read-only in fr-ra's sandbox, and there are
# no leases to keep.
pid-file=
leasefile-ro
# No log line for every advertisement sent.
quiet-ra
enable-ra
interface=eth1
dhcp-range=::,constructor:eth1,ra-only

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.adblock.dns_service) -- regenerated on every
# `apply`, do not edit by hand. A dedicated, frfw-owned dnsmasq
# instance (fr-adblock-dns.service) -- never the system's own
# dnsmasq.service/dnsmasq.conf, which this never touches.
port=53
no-resolv
no-hosts
addn-hosts=@ROOT@/etc/fr_os/adblock.hosts
interface=lo
# Each address of those interfaces, and the ones they get later (ROADMAP
# FND-1c): IPv6 addresses come and go -- the provider's prefix is
# renumbered, the stable ULA one is added by the next apply.
bind-dynamic
server=1.1.1.1
log-queries=extra
log-facility=@ROOT@/var/log/fr_os-dns/queries.log
user=nobody
group=nogroup
# No PID file: systemd tracks the process, and /run is read-only in the
# unit's sandbox (security-lessons I1). Without this dnsmasq writes
# /run/dnsmasq.pid even in the foreground.
pid-file=

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.adblock.dns_service) -- regenerated on every
# `apply`, do not edit by hand. A dedicated, frfw-owned dnsmasq
# instance (fr-adblock-dns.service) -- never the system's own
# dnsmasq.service/dnsmasq.conf, which this never touches.
port=53
no-resolv
no-hosts
addn-hosts=@ROOT@/etc/fr_os/adblock.hosts
interface=lo
interface=eth1
# Each address of those interfaces, and the ones they get later (ROADMAP
# FND-1c): IPv6 addresses come and go -- the provider's prefix is
# renumbered, the stable ULA one is added by the next apply.
bind-dynamic
server=1.1.1.1
server=9.9.9.9
user=nobody
group=nogroup
# No PID file: systemd tracks the process, and /run is read-only in the
# unit's sandbox (security-lessons I1). Without this dnsmasq writes
# /run/dnsmasq.pid even in the foreground.
pid-file=

etc/fr_os/dnsmasq_ra.conf.text:
# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# Router Advertisements on the LAN (ROADMAP FND-1b/1c), and nothing else:
# each device's /64s, for SLAAC -- the one dhcpcd gave it from the
# provider's prefix and the stable ULA one -- and, where the router's
# resolver serves the zone, the resolver's address (RDNSS).

no-hosts

allowinterfaces eth0 eth1

interface eth0

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.adblock.dns_service) -- regenerated on every

# instance (fr-adblock-dns.service) -- never the system's own
# dnsmasq.service/dnsmasq.conf, which this never touches.

no-resolv
no-hosts
addn-hosts=@ROOT@/etc/fr_os/adblock.hosts
interface=lo
interface=eth1
# Each address of those interfaces, and the ones they get later (ROADMAP
# FND-1c): IPv6 addresses come and go -- the provider's prefix is
# renumbered, the stable ULA one is added by the next apply.

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.

# for the rest of it.

noipv4

# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never

slaac private

# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1 eth1.30

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64 eth1.30/1/64

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1 eth1.30

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64 eth1.30/1/64

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1 eth1.30

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64 eth1.30/1/64

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1

interface eth0
	ipv6rs

	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64

etc/fr_os/dhcpcd6.conf.text:
# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1 eth1.30

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64 eth1.30/1/64

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.adblock.dns_service) -- regenerated on every
# `apply`, do not edit by hand. A dedicated, frfw-owned dnsmasq
# instance (fr-adblock-dns.service) -- never the system's own
# dnsmasq.service/dnsmasq.conf, which this never touches.
port=53
no-resolv
no-hosts
addn-hosts=@ROOT@/etc/fr_os/adblock.hosts
interface=lo
interface=eth1
# Each address of those interfaces, and the ones they get later (ROADMAP
# FND-1c): IPv6 addresses come and go -- the provider's prefix is

# unit's sandbox (security-lessons I1). Without this dnsmasq writes

pid-file=

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.

etc/fr_os/dhcpcd6.conf.text:
# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64

etc/fr_os/dnsmasq_adblock.conf.text:
# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.adblock.dns_service) -- regenerated on every
# `apply`, do not edit by hand. A dedicated, frfw-owned dnsmasq
# instance (fr-adblock-dns.service) -- never the system's own
# dnsmasq.service/dnsmasq.conf, which this never touches.
port=53
no-resolv
no-hosts
addn-hosts=@ROOT@/etc/fr_os/adblock.hosts
interface=lo
interface=eth1
# Each address of those interfaces, and the ones they get later (ROADMAP
# FND-1c): IPv6 addresses come and go -- the provider's prefix is
# renumbered, the stable ULA one is added by the next apply.
bind-dynamic
server=1.1.1.1
server=9.9.9.9
user=nobody
group=nogroup
# No PID file: systemd tracks the process, and /run is read-only in the
# unit's sandbox (security-lessons I1). Without this dnsmasq writes
# /run/dnsmasq.pid even in the foreground.
pid-file=

etc/fr_os/dnsmasq_ra.conf.text:
# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# Router Advertisements on the LAN (ROADMAP FND-1b/1c), and nothing else:
# each device's /64s, for SLAAC -- the one dhcpcd gave it from the
# provider's prefix and the stable ULA one -- and, where the router's
# resolver serves the zone, the resolver's address (RDNSS).

no-resolv
no-hosts

etc/fr_os/dhcpcd6.conf.text:
# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1 eth1.30

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64 eth1.30/1/64

etc/fr_os/dhcpcd6.conf.text:
# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1 eth1.30

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64 eth1.30/1/64

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.adblock.dns_service) -- regenerated on every

# instance (fr-adblock-dns.service) -- never the system's own
# dnsmasq.service/dnsmasq.conf, which this never touches.
port=53
no-resolv
no-hosts
addn-hosts=@ROOT@/etc/fr_os/adblock.hosts
interface=lo
interface=eth1

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# Router Advertisements on the LAN (ROADMAP FND-1b/1c), and nothing else:

etc/fr_os/dhcpcd6.conf.text:
# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1 eth1.30

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64 eth1.30/1/64

# dnsmasq.service/dnsmasq.conf, which this never touches.
port=53

# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.

# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64

etc/fr_os/dhcpcd6.conf.text:
# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64

# `apply`, do not edit by hand. A dedicated, frfw-owned dnsmasq
# instance (fr-adblock-dns.service) -- never the system's own
# dnsmasq.service/dnsmasq.conf, which this never touches.
port=53
no-resolv
no-hosts
addn-hosts=@ROOT@/etc/fr_os/adblock.hosts
interface=lo
interface=eth1
# Each address of those interfaces, and the ones they get later (ROADMAP
# FND-1c): IPv6 addresses come and go -- the provider's prefix is

bind-dynamic
server=1.1.1.1

user=nobody

# unit's sandbox (security-lessons I1). Without this dnsmasq writes
# /run/dnsmasq.pid even in the foreground.
pid-file=
